SKIP by deletion test. The overlap is 4 lines (strip / skip-empty / json.loads / skip JSONDecodeError); surrounding control flow is disjoint — charter_replay.decode_lines is a pure batch function (no process/pipe/clock, so recorded transcripts replay through it), trigger_eval._stream_events is a generator entangled with select(), buffer carryover, and timeout. Deleting a hypothetical shared seam re-materializes 4 trivial lines in 2 callers: complexity moves, doesn't concentrate. The seam would be shallow (interface ~ implementation; json.loads('null')->None forces a sentinel in any line-level helper). Repo rule requires observed divergence between copies — there is none; both encode the same skip-undecodable policy identically. Sharing would also cost charter_replay its pure-replay locality.
